goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: The blueprint explicitly requires Lot 0 to replace standard-memory manual approval while preserving security and destructive-action gates. Current stores, compiler, product UI/CLI, projection metadata, and normative verifiers still encode pending→approve|reject. The approved package is the largest reversible vertical slice: a calibrated deterministic policy, immutable admission attestations, additive store/runtime integration, an explicit flags-off legacy mode, exceptional quarantine resolution, projection compatibility, normative alignment, and executable AD-AC01–07 coverage. Graph, Working Memory, ontology, MCP recall, and deploy remain later dependency-ordered lots.

worker_package.objective: Implement the Lot 0 governance migration end to end. Add a versioned, deterministic memory-admission policy that accepts independently verified signals, never uses extractor self-confidence as a deciding signal, emits hash-attested `supermemory.admission-decision.v1` records for `auto_activate|activate_ttl|quarantine|discard`, and leaves verifier outages in non-recallable `pending_verification`. Add idempotent `admitCandidate` flows to both stores and governance/compiler paths; activate/project only auto/TTL decisions with valid evidence and scope, enforce TTL, keep quarantine/discard out of normal recall, and limit `reviewCandidate` to quarantines plus explicit legacy migration mode. Preserve existing v1/v2 state and active reviewed memories without rewriting immutable artifacts; flags off must retain current behavior. In explicit automatic mode, migrate the local product/API/UI/CLI from nominal approval to an Exceptions view, while keeping deletion, permissions, secrets, external actions, production readiness, and destructive ontology gates explicit. Carry admission metadata into Hindsight promotion. Align normative documentation and governance verifiers only for standard-memory activation. Add a versioned calibration/holdout corpus and deterministic tests covering AD-AC01–07, idempotence, projection ordering, workspace isolation, legacy compatibility, and the current manual path when flags are disabled. Do not implement Working Memory, graph, ontology, MCP recall, or deployment.

stop_if: Any required implementation would overwrite or discard existing user changes in the dirty worktree rather than merge around them.
Automatic activation would require trusting extractor confidence, inventing verifier results, or treating a missing/unavailable verifier as approval.

The separate holdout corpus does not demonstrate at least 95% auto-activation precision and under 5% human exceptions for standard claims; keep automatic mode disabled and stop with the measured result.
Backward compatibility would require rewriting existing immutable candidate/memory artifacts, mutating a real vault during verification, or silently reclassifying legacy pending candidates.
A new final admission decision outside `auto_activate|activate_ttl|quarantine|discard` appears necessary; `pending_verification` must remain a candidate state, not an invented admission decision.
A required change falls outside allowed_files, including Working Memory, graph, ontology, MCP recall, deploy, installer, or production infrastructure.
Any deterministic test requires Ollama, Hindsight, Graphiti, Neo4j, network access, credentials, or a real user vault.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.

findings: Blueprint lines 80–92 explicitly assign Lot 0 the README, technical design, PRD/governance fixtures, both stores, and approval-only verifiers while preserving deletion, external-action, permission, secret, readiness, and destructive-ontology gates.
Blueprint lines 219–252 and 465–467 require calibrated audited signals, four final decisions, deterministic policy authority, exceptional quarantine, and under 5% standard-claim exceptions.
Blueprint lines 1152–1158 and WM-AC20 require v1/v2 configurations and flags-off behavior to remain unchanged.
`codex-memory-governance.mjs:209-263` creates candidates and exposes only `reviewCandidate`; no policy or admission path exists.
`codex-workspace-store.mjs:193-419` persists pending candidates, accepts only approve/reject, writes owner-approved active memory, and projects it; active recall has no admission or TTL check.
`product-store.mjs:688-963,1121-1193` creates pending candidates during ingest, labels sources ready/needs-review, and activates only through binary manual review.
`codex-memory-compiler.mjs:416-491` ends at a pending candidate and has an extractor but no independent verifier or policy handoff.
`product-hindsight.mjs` hard-codes `review_status: approved`; `hindsight-promote.mjs` rejects active memories lacking that marker.
`supermemory-review.mjs` and `web/app.js:154-250` present approve/reject as the nominal workflow rather than persistent exceptions.
README and the technical design repeatedly state explicit approval/review-before-activation; `verify-memory-contracts.mjs` and the M1 verifier encode the same requirement.
No `scripts/lib/memory-admission-policy.mjs` or versioned admission calibration corpus currently exists.

Codex workspace state is additive object-based v2 and already preserves product-store v1 byte-for-byte through `legacyCompatibility`; this supports additive fields and new artifacts without rewriting old files.
Legacy approved memories must remain readable in flags-off/legacy mode. Existing pending candidates must not be bulk auto-activated without verified signals.
Review remains valid for quarantines and legacy migration; unrelated review queues and exact confirmations remain unchanged.
